subject.title: feat: add interactive launcher menu as thin wrapper over existing CLI

question: Should OpenClaw core own and ship a separate Rust launcher executable as a supported entry point for existing CLI commands?
rationale: The proposal adds a new executable, toolchain, packaging, and compatibility surface rather than repairing an established launcher contract, so implementation review cannot determine whether the permanent product boundary is desired.

options.title: Sponsor a core launcher
options.body: Approve a supported launcher surface, assign packaging and release ownership, and require the branch to be narrowed and corrected before merge.

options.title: Use existing entry points
options.body: Decline the additional executable and continue improving discoverability through the existing CLI, desktop app, installers, and dashboard surfaces.

options.title: Prototype externally
options.body: Move the launcher to a separately maintained package until usage and cross-platform support justify core ownership.

recommendation.title: Use existing entry points
recommendation.body: Decline the additional executable and continue improving discoverability through the existing CLI, desktop app, installers, and dashboard surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision spans core CLI and product entry-point ownership; the history-specific owner trail could not be completed, so this is the best low-confidence repository-level candidate.
